content.body:
The M1903 Springfield served the United States military for nearly 60 years, beginning in 1905. Initially, it was the standard infantry rifle but transitioned to the role of sniper rifle as the M1903A4. It fired the .30-06 round (7.62 x 63 mm), a round common to several US military firearms.
Though it was outfitted with different telescopic sights at times, the version in WWII Online uses the Weaver 330.
Snipers were often recruited from the finest marksman in the force. They were assigned to hit important targets. Snipers were so highly-valued and respected among themselves that they often followed their own code of ethics. Among these ethical rules was that a sniper would not kill an enemy sniper unless it was absolutely necessary.
